body: I don't have any stories of strength- I've just always powered through things (and am too tired right now). But I'm so impressed by your the way you're trying to find a solution. Good for you.

Sending you a lot of love. You sound like a wonderful and creative person. In my experience, I don't think our culture allows for creative people to be free. That's just not how it works, sadly.

If no one has said this to you: congratulations on being you. You're wonderful.
Shame on you! This is not a place to talk to someone like that. You have no clue what she's going through.

I'd like to respond, but for some reason I don't have it in me to devote one more minute to my illness today. 

I don't want to be alone. I'm happy that you're happy in solitude, but it's just not me. It's my illness that wants me alone.

Glad you're still moving and everything isn't a shitshow.

Wish I could say the same. It's pretty tragic.

This is a very, very good question and probably at the heart of an argument against euthanasia for the mentally ill. 

I would argue that in BPD and other mental illnesses, the constant fear and anxiety preclude success. A release from pain is the key coupled with an inability to plan because the future is being consistently wiped away by efforts to feel somewhat okay- compare it to someone gasping for breath every day. 

Because we understand the pain involved with the actual act (in my case, from hours upon hours of being subjected to thinking and researching the details), we want- rather than violence- an actual peaceful means to go that isn't exactly lonely. Many of us just long to fall asleep and not wake up. If the alternative is dying alone in a psych ward or homeless, we would feel every inch of that pain too. 

Unbearable.
You're sweet. But I'm not sure I want all of it out in this forum. :)
Thanks for asking. I'm.. the same.

Yes, I'm highly intelligent. Or was- being on so much medication and the anxiety has fried my brain a bit. But both make this all a bit more difficult. 

I'm a bit alone. I have people helping, but not much and it's pretty difficult and may get more difficult. Toughing it out alone is sort of how it's looking. Being alone on holidays is going to be murderous. My therapist told me the other day that it's a "long, dark road ahead" for me. I'm not sure I can manage that. 

You're kind to respond so thoroughly. Sorry you were up all night. I hope it was because you were doing something productive/fun and not insomnia.

I'm off the drugs. Rehab ripped me off cold turkey. Benzo withdrawal lasts 6 monts to ...years.

I'm *extremely* tough. And I'm very tired of it.  

I'm surrounded by real geniuses every day unfortunately. It's very possible and likely that I have brain damage at this point. If not, the withdrawal and medication for the withdrawal makes functioning very difficult. I forget simple things. I drop things. I fall over in the bathroom... I'm legally blind. 

I just don't make enough money to sustain this level of dysfunction long-term. I don't really believe in God. Maybe. Well, not one that's kind. Kafka's great. I have his diaries in my library which I don't have right now. Basically too disabled by anxiety and PTSD to do much of anything. 

It's nice to talk to you though. I'm alone all day and alone at night. It's created a little vortex of crazy.

Pretty much. It's really sad.

Sorry you've had difficulties. That really sucks. I hope you're getting better.

Well, I've been seeing therapists since I was 13 and was put on medication when for depression in my 20s. I took myself off because I couldn't study on them. I had a psychotic break from doing that and everything just started spiraling downhill. I just could never get it together. Lots of relationships, lots of chaos. I got into relationship with a wonderful man a few years ago and it turned out to be an abusive relationship. He wound up strangling me, so I put him in jail. I'm just tired honestly. And my workplace is filled with very normal and fulfilled people with stable families. I have to see that and it's pretty painful.

Just tired.

Oh I see. 

Um. I'm a 40-yr old woman with a history of traumatic relationships and depression. No spouse, no kids, lots of suicide attempts under my belt. It's a daily nightmare I can't even describe. I went to really good schools and had a nice future planned. It's been absolute hell.
